events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.83)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver, at 21:33:20 after acceptance at 21:30:00 — i.e. 3 min 20 s (200 s) after matching, and the $6.61 fee is on record [F2][F5]. NS-0 routes a rider cancellation to the NS-4 branch ("cancelled_by = rider"), so the chargeability question is governed by NS-4, not by the driver no-show provisions [F2][NS-0].

NS-4 sets the only relevant test: for an immediate booking, a rider cancellation within 3 minutes of matching is free, while a cancellation after 3 minutes makes the $6.61 fee stand [F2][NS-4]. The rider's cancellation at 200 s falls on the chargeable side of that line, so the fee is validly charged and the outcome is no_action [F2][F5][NS-4].

The rider's case instead invokes NS-1 and NS-2 [F1][F3][F4]. Those clauses only gate a driver-side no-show fee — they require the driver to have tapped "I'm Here", to be within the pickup radius, and to have waited over 3 minutes before a driver-initiated cancellation [F3][F4][NS-1]. Here the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null) and never entered the pickup radius (closest approach 2501 m), so no driver no-show fee was ever in play; their failure does not convert the rider's own post-3-minute cancellation into a refundable one [F1][F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. The rider advocate's own concession that NS-4, read as the exclusive rule for rider cancellations, leaves the fee standing is correct [F13][NS-2].

The driver's "about 5 min, traffic" message and his statement that he was en route are statements and are in any event unnecessary: NS-4 turns only on elapsed time after matching, and the timeline (acceptance 21:30:00, cancellation 21:33:20) is a system record [F2][F8][F9][NS-4]. There is no ETA-based free-cancellation rule in Ryde's policy, so the driver's not-yet-arrival is not a ground to refund; conditions were also unremarkable, with no incident recorded near the route during the window [F1][F11][F12][NS-4]. The rider's recourse is a discretionary RydeHELP appeal within 30 days, which is not a basis for a refund here [F2][NS-7].

No account flag is warranted: the NS-2 fraud limb is not engaged (no "I'm Here" tap and no arrival claim by the driver), and the driver's 90-day record shows 1081 trips with zero disputes and zero upheld findings, so NS-2's flag condition is not met [F4][F13][F14][NS-2]. The fare record shows a single $6.61 cancellation fee with surge at 1.0× and no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 yields nothing to return [F5][F6][FARE-1].

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 2501 m, and the GPS record shows he was never within 200 m of the pickup at any time before cancellation.
The platform recorded no arrival at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null), so the NS-1 (ii) condition that the driver be at the pickup location according to GPS data cannot be satisfied.
The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), so NS-1 (i) is not satisfied either.
Because at least one NS-1 condition fails — indeed all of (i) and (ii) fail — the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full.

The rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance, and the driver's own message promised "about 5 min", i.e. an arrival materially after the 3-minute mark the rider had already waited; the driver's written statement only says he "was on my way", which does not place him at the pickup point.
The driver's account shows 1081 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld, so the account-level history does not support an abuse-of-cancellation-button flag against him on this record.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled at 21:33:20, 3 min 20 s after acceptance, and under NS-4 a rider cancellation later than 3 minutes after matching normally makes the $6.61 fee stand — the other side will cite F2 (timeline) for this. My answer is that NS-0 routes a rider cancellation to NS-4, but NS-1/NS-2 govern whether the fee is properly chargeable at all on this record; if the judge reads NS-4 as the exclusive rule for rider cancellations, the fee survives.

The driver will argue he was en route and only 5 minutes out (F8, his chat message) and that the rider simply chose to cancel (F9 driver statement) — the rider's own message asking "How long will you be?" (F7) shows she was still willing to wait at 21:30. I rely on the GPS record (F1) and the null arrival / null "I'm Here" fields (F3, F4) beating the driver's statement, but a judge who weighs the driver's ETA message may find the rider cancelled too eagerly.

On this record the driver pressed no "I'm Here" (F4) and was outside the pickup radius (F1), so I cannot ask for a flag_account under NS-2's fraud limb; the weakest part of my case is that I have no positive evidence of button abuse, only absence of the arrival record.

claims.assertion: The rider's own complaint states the ground for cancellation: the driver was not at the pickup point when she cancelled, and the GPS record confirms the driver's closest approach was 2501 m, never entering the 200 m pickup radius (F1).
The cancellation was made by the rider, not the driver (F2), so the $6.61 charge falls to be assessed under the rider-cancellation branch, not the driver no-show/“I'm Here” branch.

This was an immediate booking (accepted 21:30:00) and the rider cancelled at 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s after matching — more than 3 minutes — so the $6.61 cancellation fee is validly charged (F2, F5).

The driver never tapped “I'm Here” and the platform never recorded him at the pickup point (F4, F3), so no waiting-fee or no-show finding can be made against the driver on this record — the dispute is purely the rider's post-3-minute cancellation.

The driver's conduct during the window was cooperative and transparent: he told the rider he was about 5 minutes out in traffic (F8) and his written statement confirms he was en route when the rider cancelled (F9); nothing in the chat shows refusal, abandonment or unresponsiveness.

Ryde publishes no rule allowing a rider to cancel free of charge merely because the driver has not yet arrived within 3 minutes; the driver's not-yet-arrival is therefore not a ground to refund the fee, and the rider's recourse is a manual appeal only (F12 weather/traffic conditions are not part of that rule).
Nothing in the fare record shows any unpublished or surplus add-on beyond the single $6.61 cancellation fee, with surge at 1.0× (F5, F6), so there is no overcharge to return.
The driver's 90-day record shows 1081 trips with zero disputes and zero upheld findings (F14); no account flag is warranted against him in this case.

weaknesses: The rider will press the driver's own chat message at 21:31 that he was “about 5 min” away (F8); if the true arrival was nearer 5 minutes, the rider had no realistic prospect of being picked up and will argue the fee is inequitable — although NS-4 contains no ETA-based waiver, so this is fairness argument rather than a clause.

The driver's closest approach of 2501 m at 21:31:20 (F1) is a long way from the pickup, so the rider will argue he had effectively failed to serve the booking; the counter is that he was still within the 3-minute window when she cancelled at 21:33:20 (F2) and NS-4 turns only on elapsed time after matching.
No traffic or weather fact (F10, F11, F12) supports the driver's “traffic” explanation for the delay (F8), so that part of the driver's statement is unsupported and should not be relied on.
The rider has one prior dispute in 90 days with none upheld (F13); this is weak as it is neutral-to-mildly-favourable to the rider and cannot be used to attack her credibility.

points.response: Conceded as to the facts — the driver was 2501 m away and never entered the pickup radius (F1) — but that concession runs against the driver, not for him: a driver who never reached the pickup point cannot satisfy NS-1 (i) or (ii), so no $6.61 no-show fee is chargeable on this record.

The branch argument is right on its face but misapplied: NS-0 sends a rider cancellation to NS-4, whose charge presupposes a valid cancellation event, while NS-1/NS-2 fix the fee to what the driver did; here the driver pressed no "I'm Here" (F4) and was never within 200 m (F1, F3), so the fee is not earned.

The 3 min 20 s elapsed time is not disputed (F2), but the rider had been told at 21:31 the driver was still about 5 minutes out in traffic (F8) while sitting 2501 m away (F1); NS-2 requires the fee to be refunded in full where the NS-1 arrival/"I'm Here" conditions fail (F3, F4).

This is the driver conceding my case: he accepts there is no arrival record and no "I'm Here" tap (F3, F4), which is exactly why NS-1 fails and NS-2 requires the $6.61 to be refunded rather than retained.

The "about 5 min" message (F8) speaks against the driver, not for him: it puts his own ETA at 21:36 for a 21:30 booking, and the record corroborates no progress — 2501 m closest approach at 21:31:20 (F1) and no arrival entry ever created (F3). Recorded conditions were fair with no traffic incidents (F11, F12), so the delay is unexplained.

I do not need an ETA-waiver rule, and I cite none: my case rests on NS-1/NS-2, under which the fee is chargeable only if the driver tapped "I'm Here" and was within the pickup radius, neither of which happened (F1, F3, F4).

The $6.61 is the only disputed item and it is a cancellation fee, not a published add-on, so FARE-1 does not save it; NS-2 makes the whole $6.61 refundable once the NS-1 conditions fail (F2, F3, F4, F5).

I agree no account flag is warranted against this driver on this record, and I have not requested one; the driver's 90-day history of 1081 trips with zero disputes (F14) is irrelevant to whether the $6.61 was chargeable.

The 2501 m closest approach (F1) is not in dispute and proves only that the driver had not yet arrived — it does not engage NS-1 at all, because NS-1's conditions (press “I'm Here”, be within the pickup radius, wait > 3 min) only gate a DRIVER-initiated no-show cancellation, whereas here cancelled_by = rider (F2).

A null driver_arrived_at (F3) is equally consistent with the rider simply cancelling before the driver got there — which is exactly what happened at 21:33:20 (F2); the field is a record of non-arrival, not of any driver breach, and NS-0 routes a rider cancellation to NS-4, which contains no arrival requirement.

Correct that no “I'm Here” tap is recorded (F4), and I never relied on one: the absence of a tap means no driver-side no-show claim is made, so NS-1/NS-2 never become the applicable branch (NS-0), and it is not a concession that the rider's cancellation fee is invalid.

This strands the rider's case: NS-1/NS-2 conditions are prerequisites for a DRIVER-side no-show fee, so their failure only means the rider was never charged a no-show fee — the $6.61 on record (F5) arises from her own cancellation 3 min 20 s after matching, which NS-4 makes chargeable with no_action.

The driver's “about 5 min” message (F8) is a chat statement, and under the system-record rules it cannot override the timeline: acceptance 21:30:00 and rider cancellation 21:33:20 (F2) show she left 20 seconds past the 3-minute mark, and NS-4 turns on elapsed time after matching only — no ETA-based waiver exists in Ryde's policy.

We agree on this, and it goes to the driver's benefit: 1081 trips in 90 days with zero disputes and zero upheld (F14), together with no arrival record (F3) and no “I'm Here” tap (F4), means no abuse-of-button or account flag is sought against the driver.

The rider's fairness argument gains nothing from the traffic and weather record: no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window (F11), only moderate 20–29 km/h banding on Jalan Buroh (F10) under fair skies with 0.0 mm rain (F12), so the conditions cannot be recast as an exceptional event justifying a free cancellation.

notices.text: Your cancellation fee of $6.61 stands. You cancelled 3 minutes 20 seconds after being matched with a driver, and cancellations more than 3 minutes after matching are chargeable. The driver's not having arrived doesn't change this — there's no rule that makes a cancellation free just because the driver was still on the way, and Ryde doesn't have an ETA-based free-cancellation policy. We know this isn't the answer you wanted. If you'd like it looked at again, you can ask for a discretionary RydeHELP appeal.

Good news — no action will be taken against you, and no fee was charged to you. The rider cancelled about 3 minutes 20 seconds after you were matched, which is their cancellation to own, so this wasn't treated as a no-show on your part. Nothing was added to your account, and there's no mark on your record. Your account stays in good standing, so you can keep accepting trips as usual. Thanks for driving with Ryde.
